items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-12
items.q: Nick John, Nick got in with me right after I went into... Uh, just before I went into Elmer Rockland. And he, uh, done business at Elmer Rockland.

ctx.x: So, okay, can you remember the time when you were playing with Ivan Thomas, when he was murdered? Yeah, sure. Can you tell us something about that? One thing I'd like to know is, can you remember any of the other people in the band? Yeah. Pomp. Pomp. Changer. Bruce Robinson, the piano. Walter Preston playing banjo. Chani on the drum. Steve Antonis. Uh-huh. And a young footballer named Al was playing tennis. Uh-huh. Those old boys were in that band at that time. He didn't have a bass player? No, he was using two…

School. I have a kid. Nick's symphony. His father had a grocery store. About stuff like stuff That's how I got to find it with Nick. He liked it so much, so... He liked to run a business, and he really runs a business really good. I'd better complain about Nick, but he still runs my business, right? He does not? He's alright. I mean, he's not in music. No, he's alive. He's alive. Yeah. Um, can you remember how long he was your manager, and when Dorothy Tate took over? Can you remember, I've never been able to…

된 된 된 된 된 That's right. Joe Peck. Peck. Peck. They call him Joe Peck. He's got a place on our own. He's a big old gal dressed. Joe Peck. And his brother Frank. And after I left there, I didn't... I didn't wait out for him no more, because I'm here. It's a casual. It was a rough idea. I wouldn't make any money. This was all in the 30s? Who was you playing with at the Popeye's? Yeah, it was... items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: Nick Gagliano, which is a lawyer now, saw that we had a uniform.

ctx.x: You had him in a few hours after you had him out with the ventures.

As soon as they pulled them, the lads out, they put them in. And then I had to go to the dentist every day. And for about three or four days, three days, and he told me to take them out myself. He showed them how to do. And I would get in the middle of bed because the gum was sore. And for dear At concerts I really stand, I really stand, the play of soul. You know the play, if you play at a concert, because you got a certain amount of time, it's not like staying in the hall, you know, 45 minutes, probably you…
Yes. As far as the tone itself.
